title: Non-coding variant effect prediction · Tuesday, November 24

transcript.text: This is the Paper Library daily on Non-coding variant effect prediction, for Tuesday, November 24.
Let's turn to non-coding variant effect prediction, where both new papers are bioRxiv preprints about scoring variants.

The first comes from the Hassanien lab. It looks at non-canonical splicing variants, which sit outside the conserved dinucleotides at splice junctions and are hard to interpret. A disruption score alone doesn't tell you the splice outcome or how uncertain the call is.

Their framework, SpliceVarMech, compares wild-type and mutant sequences, generates candidate splice outcomes with discrete sequence diffusion, and uses Bayesian inference to give disruption probabilities with credible intervals, plus the predicted mechanism.

On 31 validated variants from male infertility genes, it reached an AUROC of 1.0, against 0.62 for SpliceAI, the best of 16 tools. Fine-tuning on BRCA1 saturation genome editing data raised discrimination from 0.72 to 0.84 on 203 held-out variants.
That perfect score comes from just 31 variants, and the authors note calibration was only checked in-sample. The BRCA1 result is the more convincing test.

The second paper, from the Haldar lab, benchmarks six genomic foundation models on about 7,000 ClinVar variants in ten limb-girdle muscular dystrophy genes, comparing frozen embeddings, fine-tuning and context lengths.
Evo2 led, with an MCC of 0.86 and an AUROC of 0.96 at 501 base pairs of context. Longer context helped five of the six models, but fine-tuning helped only three and hurt the other three.
The native scores from GPN-Star and AlphaGenome did even better, with MCCs around 0.93 and 0.94. But the labels track annotation category quite strongly, and clinical usefulness hasn't been tested.
So the takeaway is that sequence context and careful adaptation matter, but in both papers the benchmarks are still too small or too label-biased to show these tools are ready for the clinic.

papers.title: Genomic foundation models and complementary variant-scoring strategies in LGMD-associated genes: architecture, adaptation, and sequence context
SpliceVarMech: A causal generative framework for mechanistic interpretation of non-canonical splicing variants
papers.authors: Moustafa Zein and Aboul Ella Hassanien
